questions.question: Q: What is the difference between apparent and absolute magnitude?

points.text: Apparent magnitude is how bright a star looks from Earth. Absolute magnitude is the brightness it would have if placed at a standard distance of 10 parsecs.

questions.question: Q: State the spectral classes from hottest to coolest.

points.text: O, B, A, F, G, K, M (mnemonic: Oh Be A Fine Girl/Guy, Kiss Me).

questions.question: Q: How is stellar parallax used to measure distance?

points.text: A star's apparent shift against background stars is measured over 6 months. Distance in parsecs = 1/parallax angle in arcseconds.

questions.question: Q: Why do blue stars appear brighter than red stars of the same size?

points.text: Blue stars are hotter, and luminosity depends on temperature (L ∝ T⁴), so hotter stars emit far more energy per unit area.

questions.question: Q: What is the inverse square law of light?

points.text: Apparent brightness decreases proportionally to 1/d², where d is the distance from the star.
